title: Rational smooth inverse systems of principal singularity pairs
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-per-principal-singularity-pair]. A rational smooth pair system for $(X,I)$ consists of a nonempty small directed partially ordered set $A$; an inverse diagram $D:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathit{Sch}$; ideal sheaves $I_a$ such that each $(D_a,I_a)$ is a principal singularity pair [def-per-principal-singularity-pair]; compatible finite-type $\mathbf Q$-structure morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; affine smooth transition morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] extending the distinguished ideals; and a limit cone with vertex $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, applied dually], whose projections extend each $I_a$ to $I$ and are regular [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism]. For each $m\geq0$ the data include the canonical thick-fibre diagram, with its objects identified by specified isomorphisms with $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O(D_a)/I_a^m)$, its natural closed immersions into $D$, and the compatible cone with vertex $(I^m).\mathrm{subscheme}$; the projection squares commute with the closed immersions. Powers and their closed subschemes are those of [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. For $m\geq1$ this cone is a limit cone and all its projections are regular. The distinguished ideal on a thick fibre is the extension of $I_a$ along its closed immersion, and for an open $U\subseteq D_a$, its thick-fibre open is the inverse image $U\cap D_{a,m}$.

source.place: Temkin, Non-embedded Desingularization, proof of Proposition 3.3.5, printed p.25; finite disjoint unions as in §2.1.14
